headline: Record profit and revenue extend RJF's growth streak
summary_short: Raymond James reported revenue of $4.36B (+2.3% q/q, +13.5% y/y) and net income of $595M (+36.5% y/y) for the quarter ended June 30, 2026; diluted EPS was $3.01, up from $2.12 a year ago.
summary_long: Total revenues were $4.36B (+13.5% y/y, +2.3% q/q); the company's own net-revenues measure (after interest expense) was $3.93B, a record, up 16% y/y on higher asset-management fees (~$2.1B) and the newly closed Clark Capital acquisition. Net income rose to $595M (+36.5% y/y, +9.4% q/q) and diluted EPS to $3.01, helped q/q by a lower 20.7% effective tax rate versus 26.0% last quarter. Capital Markets revenue rose 25% y/y on stronger M&A/advisory and underwriting activity. Bank segment net interest margin slipped to 2.71% (-3bp y/y, -10bp q/q) as net bank loans grew 13% y/y to $56.2B. The firm bought back $400M of stock; CET1 stood at 21.6%. Total cash fell 11.1% q/q to $9.98B; shareholders' equity rose to $12.70B.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes the increase mainly to growth in asset management and related administrative fees, which rose to roughly $2.1 billion this quarter.
Company says the q/q net income gain was largely due to a lower effective tax rate, which fell to 20.7% from 26.0% the prior quarter.
CEO Paul Shoukry pointed to strength in the Private Client Group's fee-based assets, robust advisor recruiting, and strong investment-banking pipelines as tailwinds entering the next quarter.
